thesis.claim: How fast brains change decides how soon evolution stops, not where. In B2 at 10,000 tokens, with brains changed only when they are copied, the brains of iteration 1,500 tie whatever the rate of change they evolved under: for every pair of the mutation probabilities 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4 and 0.8, the brains of one rate hold between 45% and 55% of a world contested with the other's, in the median seed. And every rate has stopped by then: the brains of iteration 1,500 hold between 45% and 55% against those of iteration 1,000 of the same world.
thesis.why: Chapter 53 reads the end of evolution as the end of a game: a contest for nodes has a best way to play — be unpredictable — and once a population plays it, nothing better exists to be selected. If that is right, every world that varies enough to find it ends in the same place, and the rate of change only sets how fast it gets there (selection finds the answer). The two other pictures of Chapter 43 predict otherwise: in a mutation-selection balance (Haldane 1927) the brains of a faster-changing world carry more damage at any moment and lose to those of a slower one, the more the faster; past an error threshold (Eigen 1971) the fastest world loses what it learned altogether. No pilot has varied the rate in B2. In B1 two pilots at 10,000 tokens (seed 1, 600 iterations) found births of 2.0, 2.9 and 8.0 per hundred agents at 0.05, 0.2 and 0.8 — a balance in a world whose brains are nearly blind. In B2 births are held at one in a hundred by old age (Chapter 52), so the question moves from how often agents breed to how good their brains become.
thesis.confirm: For each of the ten pairs of rates, in each seed, the brains of iteration 1,500 of one rate play those of the other twice — once in each rate's world of that seed at iteration 1,500 (gol_tournament.contest); a pair's score is the mean share of the second rate's brains; the median over the ten seeds lies between 0.45 and 0.55 for all ten pairs. And in each of the five conditions, the median world's score of iteration 1,500 against iteration 1,000 (two contests) lies between 0.45 and 0.55.
thesis.refute: A pair of rates outside 0.45 to 0.55 in the median seed: the rate of change decides how good the brains become — by damage that grows with the rate if the slower rate wins, by too little variation if the faster wins. Or a condition still improving after iteration 1,000 (above 0.55): that rate has not stopped.
